questions.question: Distinguish between poverty and inequality, and name one way each is measured.
questions.expected_answer: Poverty: not having enough income or resources to meet basic needs; measured with poverty lines such as the food poverty line. Inequality: the unequal distribution of income and wealth between people; measured with the Gini coefficient (0 = perfect equality, 1 = perfect inequality).

questions.question: Explain two historical causes of socio-economic imbalances in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Any two: colonial dispossession of land and cattle; 1913 Natives Land Act restricted black land ownership to about 7% (later 13%); Group Areas Act and forced removals moved people far from jobs; Bantu Education gave inferior schooling; job reservation kept skilled jobs for white workers; pass laws and migrant labour; homelands starved of investment.

questions.question: Give two present-day causes of inequality and two effects on communities.
questions.expected_answer: Causes (any two): high unemployment; unequal quality of education and skills; distance from jobs and services; slow economic growth; corruption and poor service delivery; health challenges. Effects (any two): hunger and malnutrition; ill health; children trapped in poverty; crime and social tension; protests; wasted talent.
